title_en: Several Opinions of the Leading Group for the Prevention of Juvenile Delinquency under the Central Committee for Comprehensive Social Management, the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of Justice, and the Central Committee of the Communist Youth League on Further Establishing and Improving the Supporting Work System for Handling Juvenile Criminal Cases
keywords_en: Improving the handling of criminal cases involving minors
full_text_en:
Central Comprehensive Management Committee for Prevention of Juvenile Delinquency Leading Group

Supreme People's Court Supreme People's Procuratorate

Ministry of Public Security Ministry of Justice Central Committee of the Communist Youth League

Several Opinions on Further Establishing and Perfecting the Supporting Work System for Handling Juvenile Criminal Cases

[2010] No. 1, Joint Document of the Central Comprehensive Management Committee for Prevention of Juvenile Delinquency Leading Group

In order to further implement the policy of "education, persuasion, and redemption" for minors who violate the law or commit crimes and the principle of "education as the main focus, punishment as supplementary," implement the "Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Minors," the "Law of the People's Republic of China on the Prevention of Juvenile Delinquency," and the criminal policy of "combining leniency with severity," and perfect China's juvenile justice system, the following opinions are hereby put forward on several issues concerning further establishing and perfecting the mutually supporting work system for handling juvenile criminal cases.

I. Further Establishing, Consolidating, and Perfecting Specialized Institutions for Handling Juvenile Criminal Cases

Establishing and perfecting specialized institutions for handling juvenile criminal cases is an important guarantee for doing a good job in juvenile judicial protection, preventing, correcting, and reducing juvenile delinquency. Public security organs, people's procuratorates, people's courts, and judicial administrative organs at all levels should attach full importance to and strengthen the construction of specialized institutions and specialized teams for handling juvenile criminal cases.

1. The Ministry of Public Security, provincial, and prefectural/municipal public security organs should designate corresponding agencies to be responsible for guiding the handling of juvenile criminal cases. District and county level public security organs should generally set up specialized teams for handling juvenile criminal cases within police stations and criminal investigation departments; where the number of juvenile criminal cases is small, specialized personnel may be designated to handle them.

2. The Supreme People's Procuratorate and provincial people's procuratorates should establish specialized institutions to guide the handling of juvenile criminal cases. Prefectural/municipal people's procuratorates and district/county people's procuratorates should generally establish specialized institutions or specialized teams for handling juvenile criminal cases; where conditions are insufficient, specialized personnel may be designated to handle them.

3. The Supreme People's Court and Higher People's Courts should establish a Juvenile Court Work Office. Intermediate People's Courts and Basic People's Courts should generally establish specialized institutions for adjudicating juvenile criminal cases; where conditions are insufficient, specialized personnel may be designated to handle them.

4. The Ministry of Justice and provincial judicial administrative organs should strengthen guidance on the supporting work for handling juvenile criminal cases and establish relevant work guidance groups. Legal aid institutions under the prefectural/municipal and district/county level judicial administrative organs should establish juvenile legal aid affairs departments, responsible for organizing the handling of legal aid matters for minors; where conditions are insufficient, specialized personnel may be designated to handle them. Community correction work departments of judicial administrative organs should generally set up specialized teams or designate specialized persons to be responsible for juvenile community correction work.

5. Public security organs, people's procuratorates, people's courts, and judicial administrative organs at all levels should select personnel with good political and professional qualities, who are familiar with the characteristics of minors, and who possess knowledge of criminology, sociology, psychology, pedagogy, and other fields, to handle juvenile criminal cases, and should pay attention to improving the professional level of relevant personnel through enhanced training and guidance. For specialized personnel handling juvenile criminal cases, performance indicators different from those for handling adult criminal cases should be adopted for assessment based on the specific work content.

6. In areas where conditions permit, specialized institutions handling juvenile criminal cases may, based on actual circumstances, handle criminal cases where the victim is a minor.

II. Further Strengthening the Protection of the Legitimate Rights and Interests of Minors Involved in Cases

In handling juvenile criminal cases, strengthening the protection of minors involved in cases is an objective requirement for safeguarding human rights and achieving judicial fairness, and is a necessity for ensuring the smooth progress of criminal proceedings. Public security organs, people's procuratorates, people's courts, and judicial administrative organs at all levels should actively take effective measures at all stages of handling juvenile criminal cases to respect and safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of minors involved in cases.

(1) Protection of the Legitimate Rights and Interests of Juvenile Suspects, Defendants, and Offenders

1. When handling juvenile criminal cases, without violating legal provisions, the approach should be conducted in the manner most beneficial to the minor and suitable for the minor's physical and mental characteristics, fully safeguarding the legitimate rights and interests of the minor.

2. During the process of handling juvenile criminal cases, attention should be paid to protecting the reputation of the minor and respecting the personal dignity of the minor. News reports, television programs, public publications, the internet, etc., shall not disclose or disseminate the minor's name, residence, photos, images, or other materials that could potentially identify the minor.

For units that violate this provision, radio and television management, news publishing, and other departments should propose handling opinions and take corresponding actions.

3. When handling juvenile criminal cases, on the premise of handling the case in accordance with legal procedures and ensuring the quality of case handling, the case should be processed as quickly as possible to reduce the adverse impact of criminal proceedings on the minor.

4. In cases where a minor and an adult jointly commit a crime, the cases should generally be prosecuted and adjudicated separately; for cases where separate handling is not appropriate due to special circumstances, appropriate protective measures should be taken for the minor.

5. When a juvenile suspect or defendant is interrogated or tried in court, their legal representative should be notified to be present. After verifying the identity without error, the detention center should allow the legal representative to enter the interrogation site together with the case handlers.

After the adoption of compulsory measures such as criminal detention or arrest against a minor, unless circumstances hinder the investigation or notification is impossible, the legal representative or family members should be notified within 24 hours.

If the legal representative cannot be present or is not suitable to be present, with the consent of the juvenile suspect or defendant or according to their wishes, other close relatives, friends, social workers, teachers, lawyers, and other suitable adults may be notified to be present.

When interrogating a juvenile suspect or defendant, a detailed interrogation outline should be formulated based on the characteristics of the minor and the circumstances of the case, conducted in a manner suitable for the minor, and the language used in interrogation should be accurate and easy to understand. During interrogation, they should be informed of their procedural rights under the law, informed of the legal provisions and significance of truthful confessions of case facts, verified whether they have shown signs of voluntary surrender, meritorious service, reporting others' crimes, etc., and their confessions of guilt or defenses of innocence or lesser guilt should be heard. Interrogation of female juvenile suspects or defendants should be conducted by or with the participation of female case handlers. Generally, restraints should not be used when interrogating a juvenile suspect or defendant; if restraints are truly necessary due to personal dangerousness, they should be immediately removed once the actual danger is eliminated.

6. When handling juvenile criminal cases, combined with social investigations into the background of the juvenile suspect, attention should be paid to hearing the opinions of the minor themselves, their legal representatives, defense counsel, victims, and other relevant parties. Attention should be paid to whether the juvenile suspect or defendant was coerced, and whether there was any adult instigation of the crime, teaching of criminal methods, or use of the minor to commit the crime.

7. When public security organs handle juvenile criminal cases, they should give priority to considering the application of non-custodial compulsory measures for minors and strengthen effective supervision; custodial compulsory measures should be used cautiously in accordance with the law, with stricter conditions compared to adults. The rate of criminal detention, arrest, or prosecution shall not be used as a performance assessment indicator for handling juvenile criminal cases.

Detained minors should be held and managed separately from adults. Conditional detention centers may set up specialized juvenile wards. Conditional detention centers may also distinguish and hold and manage detained minors based on the severity and type of alleged crime.

If, after being admitted to the detention center, a juvenile suspect or defendant complies with management, a change of compulsory measures will not pose a risk to society, and normal progress of the proceedings can be ensured, the public security organ, people's procuratorate, or people's court should promptly change the compulsory measures; the detention center should request the relevant case-handling department to handle other non-custodial compulsory measures.

At the first interrogation of a juvenile suspect or from the date of adopting compulsory measures, the public security organ should inform the minor and their legal representative of the relevant procedural rights and obligations. While informing them of their right to entrust a defender, they should also be informed that if they have financial difficulties, they may apply for legal aid from a legal aid institution, and procedural guarantees should be provided.

8. When people's procuratorates handle juvenile criminal cases, they should interrogate the juvenile suspect, insist on making fewer arrests and being cautious about prosecution in accordance with the law. For juvenile criminal cases that must be prosecuted, if it is found that the juvenile defendant has statutory mitigating or extenuating circumstances and shows remorse, a suggestion for a lighter or mitigated punishment should be made; if the statutory conditions for probation are met, a sentencing recommendation for probation should be clearly made. The rate of approval of arrests, prosecution, etc., shall not be used as a performance assessment indicator for handling juvenile criminal cases.

During the stages of reviewing arrest approval and reviewing prosecution, the people's procuratorate should inform the juvenile suspect and their legal representative of the relevant procedural rights and obligations. While informing them of their right to entrust a defender, they should also be informed that if they have financial difficulties, they may apply for legal aid from a legal aid institution, and procedural guarantees should be provided.

People's procuratorates should strengthen legal supervision over the investigation, adjudication, supervision, and execution of sentences in juvenile criminal cases, establish a long-term supervision mechanism, and effectively prevent and correct illegal handling of cases and acts infringing upon the legitimate rights and interests of minors.

9. If a juvenile suspect or their legal representative expresses the intention to entrust a defense counsel but has not done so due to financial difficulties or other reasons, the public security organ or people's procuratorate should, in accordance with the law, provide assistance for their application for legal aid.

If a juvenile defendant who is under the age of 18 at the time of trial has not entrusted a defense counsel, the people's court should designate a lawyer undertaking legal aid obligations to provide defense.

10. For juvenile criminal cases where the defendant is under the age of 16 at the time of trial, the trial shall not be conducted in public. For juvenile criminal cases where the defendant is between 16 and 18 years old at the time of trial, the trial generally shall not be conducted in public; if it is necessary to conduct an open trial, it must be approved by the president of the people's court at the same level, and the number and scope of observers should be appropriately restricted.

11. Detention centers, juvenile correctional facilities, and community correction work departments of judicial administrative organs should understand the physical and mental characteristics of juvenile offenders serving sentences, strengthen psychological counseling, carry out activities beneficial to the physical and mental health of minors, conduct individualized education and correction, and appropriately relax conditions for applying for commutation of sentence and parole compared to adults.

12. For legal aid applications from juvenile suspects, defendants, and their legal representatives, legal aid institutions should prioritize review; if the conditions are met after review, legal aid should be provided. If the people's court designates a defender for a juvenile defendant, the legal aid institution should provide legal aid.

(2) Protection of the Legitimate Rights and Interests of Minor Victims and Witnesses

1. When handling juvenile criminal cases, attention should be paid to protecting the legitimate rights and interests of minor victims, and to providing psychological counseling and self-protection education for minor victims.

2. When handling juvenile criminal cases, attention should be paid to protecting the reputation of minor victims and respecting the personal dignity of minor victims. News reports, television programs, public publications, the internet, etc., shall not disclose or disseminate the name, residence, photos, images, or other materials that could potentially identify the minor victim.

For units that violate this provision, radio and television management, news publishing, and other departments should propose handling opinions and take corresponding actions.

3. When questioning minor victims or witnesses, especially victims of sexual crimes, a place conducive to the minor should be selected in accordance with the law, a gentle questioning method should be used, and the legal representative should be notified to be present.

Questioning of victims of sexual crimes should generally be conducted by or in the presence of female case handlers.

If the legal representative cannot be present or is not suitable to be present, with the consent of the minor victim or witness or according to their wishes, relevant adults may be notified to be present. Attention should be paid to avoiding potential adverse physical and psychological effects caused by inappropriate questioning methods.

4. When handling juvenile criminal cases, minor victims and their legal representatives should be informed of their procedural rights and obligations and methods of participation in the proceedings. Except where it may hinder the handling of the case, minor victims and their legal representatives should be informed of the progress of the case and the outcome of the case handling, and relevant circumstances should be explained.

For juvenile criminal cases that may not be filed, may be dismissed, result in non-prosecution, or result in non-custodial sentences, the opinions of the victim and their legal representative should be heard.

5. If a minor victim or their legal representative expresses the intention to entrust an agent ad litem but has not done so due to financial difficulties or other reasons, the public security organ, people's procuratorate, or people's court should assist them in applying for legal aid, and the legal aid institution should provide legal aid in accordance with the law.

6. Minor victims or witnesses, with the permission of the people's court, may generally not testify in court; or may testify in court after taking corresponding protective measures.

7. Public security organs, people's procuratorates, people's courts, and judicial administrative organs should promote reconciliation between juvenile suspects, defendants, or offenders and victims. They may regard the juvenile suspect, defendant, or offender's compensation for the victim's economic losses, obtaining the victim's understanding, etc., as a basis for lenient treatment or commutation of sentence or parole.

III. Further Strengthening Coordination and Cooperation Among Public Security Organs, People's Procuratorates, People's Courts, and Judicial Administrative Organs

The work mechanism of mutual coordination and cooperation established among public security organs, people's procuratorates, people's courts, and judicial administrative organs in handling juvenile criminal cases is an important component of China's juvenile justice system, and is also an objective need for better safeguarding the legitimate rights and interests of minors and preventing and reducing juvenile delinquency. To this end, public security organs, people's procuratorates, people's courts, and judicial administrative organs at all levels should pay attention to the connection and cooperation at each stage of the work, and further establish and perfect supporting work systems.

(1) Social Investigation of Juvenile Suspects and Defendants

When handling juvenile criminal cases and executing sentences, public security organs, people's procuratorates, people's courts, and judicial administrative organs should comprehensively consider the facts of the case and the content of the social investigation report.

1. The social investigation shall be the responsibility of the community correction work department of the judicial administrative organ at the place of domicile or residence of the juvenile suspect or defendant. The community correction work department of the judicial administrative organ may conduct the social investigation jointly with relevant departments, or entrust the Communist Youth League organization or other social organizations to assist in the investigation.

The social investigation agency shall investigate the juvenile suspect's personality characteristics, family situation, social interactions, growth experience, whether there are effective supervision conditions or social assistance and education measures, and behavior before and after suspected criminal conduct, and prepare a written report.

If social investigation cannot be conducted because the suspect does not provide their true name, address, or identity is unknown, the social investigation agency shall make a written explanation.

2. When public security organs handle juvenile criminal cases, they should collect evidence concerning the suspect's behavior during the case handling period or evidence on the necessity of arrest, and promptly notify the community correction work department of the judicial administrative organ to conduct a social investigation; after receiving the social investigation report made by the social investigation agency, they should carefully review it, synthesize the case circumstances, and decide whether to request approval of arrest or transfer for prosecution.

When public security organs request the people's procuratorate to review approval of arrest or transfer for prosecution in juvenile criminal cases, they should include materials on the suspect's behavior during the case handling period and the social investigation report reviewed by the public security organ with the transfer to the people's procuratorate. If the community correction work department cannot conduct a social investigation or cannot provide a written explanation of the social investigation report within the specified period, such materials should also be transferred to the people's procuratorate along with the case.

3. When people's procuratorates handle juvenile criminal cases, they should carefully review the social investigation report or written explanation of the inability to conduct a social investigation, materials on behavior during the case handling period, etc., transferred by the public security organ, comprehensively grasp the case circumstances and the physical and mental characteristics of the minor, and use them as reference for education and case handling. If the public security organ did not transfer the above materials with the case, the people's procuratorate may request the public security organ to provide them, and the public security organ shall provide them.

When people's procuratorates initiate public prosecution in juvenile criminal cases, the social investigation report, materials on behavior during the case handling period, etc., should be transferred to the people's court along with the case.

4. When people's courts handle juvenile criminal cases, they should comprehensively review the social investigation report or written explanation of the inability to conduct a social investigation, materials on behavior during the case handling period, etc., transferred by the people's procuratorate, and use the social investigation report as reference for education and sentencing. If the people's procuratorate did not transfer the above materials with the case, the people's court may request the people's procuratorate to provide them, and the people's procuratorate shall provide them.

After the judgment becomes effective, the people's court should promptly transfer the social investigation report, materials on behavior during the case handling period, etc., together with the sentence execution document, to the executing organ.

5. When executing sentences, the executing organ should conduct individualized education and correction for juvenile offenders based on the social investigation report, materials on behavior during the case handling period, etc. If the people's court did not transfer the above materials with the case, the executing organ may request the people's court to transfer them, and the people's court shall transfer them.

6. The community correction work departments of judicial administrative organs, Communist Youth League organizations, or other social organizations should accept the entrustment of public security organs, people's procuratorates, and people's courts to undertake social investigations of minors and feasibility assessments of community correction, and promptly complete and provide feedback on the investigation and assessment results.

During the social investigation process, public security organs, people's procuratorates, and people's courts should provide necessary convenience for social investigators.

(2) Verification and Review of the Age of Juvenile Suspects and Defendants

1. When public security organs handle juvenile criminal cases, they should ascertain the actual age of the juvenile suspect at the time of the crime, paying attention to the age according to the lunar calendar, registered household age, actual age, and other circumstances. In particular, whether the juvenile suspect has reached the critical ages of 14, 16, or 18 years should be verified as important case facts.

When public security organs transfer a juvenile criminal case to the people's procuratorate for review of arrest approval or review of prosecution, they should attach evidence that the juvenile suspect has reached the age of criminal responsibility. If there is insufficient evidence to prove that the juvenile suspect had reached the statutory age of criminal responsibility at the time of the crime and it is truly impossible to ascertain, the public security organ should, in accordance with the law, make a determination and handling favorable to the minor.

2. When handling juvenile criminal cases, if the People's Procuratorate finds that age evidence is missing or insufficient, or if the juvenile suspect or his or her legal representative challenges the age evidence based on relevant evidence, and such circumstances may affect the case determination, during review of arrest approval, the People's Procuratorate shall require the public security authority to supplement evidence. If the public security authority cannot provide sufficient evidence, the People's Procuratorate shall make a decision not to approve arrest and notify the public security authority to conduct supplementary investigation. During the review and prosecution process, the case shall be returned to the public security authority for supplementary investigation or investigated by the procuratorate itself. If supplementary investigation still cannot prove that the juvenile had reached the statutory age of criminal responsibility at the time of the offense, the People's Procuratorate shall make a determination and disposition favorable to the juvenile suspect in accordance with the law.

3. When a People's Court hears a juvenile criminal case initiated by public prosecution, it shall focus on examining the age evidence of the juvenile defendant. If the age evidence of the juvenile defendant is missing or insufficient, the court shall notify the People's Procuratorate to supplement or verify the evidence. If the People's Procuratorate deems further supplementary investigation necessary and submits a proposal to the People's Court, the court may postpone the trial in accordance with the law. If there is insufficient evidence to prove that the defendant had reached the statutory age of criminal responsibility at the time of the alleged crime and the truth cannot be ascertained despite efforts, the People's Court shall make a determination and disposition favorable to the juvenile defendant in accordance with the law.

(3) Education and Correction of Juvenile Suspects and Defendants

1. When handling juvenile criminal cases and executing penalties, public security authorities, People's Procuratorates, People's Courts, and judicial administrative organs shall, in light of the specific facts of the case, adopt methods suited to the physical and mental characteristics of juveniles and carry out targeted education, rehabilitation, and rescue efforts.

For juveniles who are not placed on file due to minor criminal circumstances, whose cases are dismissed, who are not prosecuted, or who are sentenced to non-custodial penalties or exempted from criminal punishment, the public security authorities, People's Procuratorates, and People's Courts shall, depending on the circumstances of the case, administer reprimands, order them to sign a statement of repentance, apologize, order compensation, etc., and require the legal representatives or other guardians to strengthen supervision. At the same time, the public security authorities, People's Procuratorates, and People's Courts shall cooperate with relevant departments to implement social assistance, education, employment, and livelihood security matters, and conduct follow-up visits and inspections as appropriate.

For juveniles who are not subject to criminal punishment because they have not reached the age of criminal responsibility, the legal representatives or other guardians shall be ordered to discipline them and arrange their education. If the school, legal representatives, or other guardians are unable or ineffective in disciplining them, and it is appropriate to send them to a specialized school, they may be sent to a specialized school in accordance with relevant regulations. When necessary, they may be placed in correctional facilities in accordance with relevant laws.

2. Public security authorities shall cooperate with the community corrections work departments of judicial administrative organs to carry out community corrections work, establish coordination mechanisms, effectively supervise juvenile community correctional offenders, take disciplinary measures against juvenile community correctional offenders who violate community correction management regulations, such as being out of control or missing supervision, and promptly handle juvenile community correctional offenders who commit new illegal or criminal acts in accordance with the law. People's Procuratorates shall exercise legal supervision over community corrections activities.

3. When People's Procuratorates dispatch personnel to appear in court to prosecute crimes in accordance with the law, they shall, at the appropriate time, provide education to the juvenile defendant.

4. During the trial of juvenile criminal cases, after the court investigation and debate have concluded, the People's Court shall, based on the specific circumstances of the case, organize the participants in the proceedings present in court to educate the juvenile defendant. For juveniles sentenced to non-custodial penalties, the People's Court shall promptly deliver the relevant legal documents, after the judgment takes effect, to the community corrections work department of the judicial administrative organ at the juvenile's registered domicile or place of residence.

5. Juvenile correctional facilities may further develop trial work-study programs. For juvenile offenders granted temporary execution of sentence outside prison or parole, the juvenile correctional facility shall promptly deliver materials such as the social investigation report and the record of behavior during imprisonment to the community corrections work department of the judicial administrative organ at the juvenile's registered domicile or place of residence.

6. Community corrections work departments of judicial administrative organs shall, with the cooperation and support of public security authorities, be responsible for the supervision, management, education, and correction of juvenile community correctional offenders, and shall carry out daily correction, behavior assessment, assistance, support, and penalty execution recommendations for juvenile community correctional offenders.

Juvenile community correctional offenders shall receive education and correction as the primary focus, and shall be separated from adults.

For juvenile community correctional offenders whose parole or probation is revoked, the community corrections work department of the judicial administrative organ shall promptly deliver materials such as the juvenile's social investigation report and record of behavior during community corrections to the local competent public security authority and People's Procuratorate.

7. Judicial administrative organs at all levels shall intensify efforts in resettlement and assistance, strengthen communication and cooperation with communities, labor and social security, education, civil affairs, the Communist Youth League, and other departments and organizations, and effectively carry out education, training, employment, eradication of bad habits, adaptation to social life, and livelihood security for juveniles released after completing sentences or after rehabilitation through re-education through labor.

8. The files of juvenile offenders shall be strictly confidential, and an effective file management system shall be established. For juveniles who have committed illegal acts or minor offenses, regions with the capacity may pilot a system for the elimination of administrative penalty and minor criminal records. Unless there are statutory reasons, the records of administrative penalties, criminal case filing, criminal compulsory measures, non-prosecution, or sentences for minor crimes of juveniles shall not be made public.

IV. Establishing a Sound Coordination and Supervision Mechanism for Supporting Work in Handling Juvenile Criminal Cases

Establishing a sound coordination and supervision mechanism for supporting work in handling juvenile criminal cases, and carrying out standardized and orderly coordination and supervision work, is an important measure to promote the construction of a juvenile justice support work system and form a joint work force.

1. Leading groups for the prevention of juvenile delinquency at all levels shall serve as the comprehensive coordination bodies for supporting work in handling juvenile criminal cases, and shall regularly convene juvenile justice work joint meetings to promptly study and coordinate the resolution of existing problems and difficulties, and summarize and promote mature and effective work experience.

2. Leading groups for the prevention of juvenile delinquency at all levels shall coordinate with relevant departments and social organizations to address issues concerning the education, employment, and livelihood security of juveniles receiving assistance.

3. The leading group for the prevention of juvenile delinquency shall be responsible for annually evaluating the performance of public security authorities, People's Procuratorates, People's Courts, and judicial administrative organs in implementing the "Opinions" and building the juvenile justice system. The evaluation results shall be incorporated into the target assessment system for Peaceful Construction and comprehensive social management. Advanced collectives and individuals that emerge in the process of handling juvenile criminal cases shall be commended.

August 28, 2010
